clue.text: Imprisonment? So it's thought

definitions.meaning: whimsically, the removal of one's liberty, a ..., as being locked up does; the question mark flags the pun
careful consideration and weighing up, the act of thinking something through

explanation.surface: A philosophical musing on whether being locked up is merely a state of mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as DE- plus LIBERATION it is loss of freedom, as in jail; read normally it means careful reflection.

clue.text: Goes off to place many a dispenser around the City

indicators.note: the dispenser pieces are placed around the City, so they enclose it

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
MPS stands for Member of the Pharmaceutical Society, a qualified pharmacist who dispenses medicines
EC is the postal district of the City of London

explanation.surface: Someone leaves to install lots of dispensers around the City of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts D, A and MPS round EC, giving D-EC-A-MPS. The City of London is the financial district, postcode EC.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to leave suddenly, to clear off or depart.

clue.text: In general one respects the individualist

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words general one respects, spanning them

explanation.surface: A remark that people generally admire the person who goes their own way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' signals the run of letters inside generaL ONE Respects.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person who prefers to act alone is an individualist.

clue.text: Support the boards — but only behind the scenes

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
the boards is a theatrical term for the stage

explanation.surface: A theatre patron backs a production but only in a hidden role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boards' is old theatrical slang for the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Backstage is the area out of the audience's sight, hence out of public view.

clue.text: Control for a bit

definitions.meaning: a check or restraint, as in keeping a tight hold on something
the strap attached to a horse's bit, used by the rider to steer

explanation.surface: Someone is told to keep things in check for a short time.
explanation.definitionFit: A rein is a means of restraint, and also the leather strap fastened to the bit in a horse's mouth.

clue.text: This little swine went to church!

definitions.text: This little swine went to church!

parts.words: This little swine went to church!
parts.note: plays on the nursery rhyme about the little pig that went to market; this one was the tenth pig handed over to the parish church as its due

explanation.surface: A twist on the nursery rhyme in which the little pig goes to church instead of market.
explanation.walkthrough: A tithe was a tenth of produce owed to the church; the piglet given up was this one.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the tithe system every tenth piglet of a litter was given to the parson as a church levy.

clue.text: Oxygen — hard to smell

parts.note: O is the chemical symbol for oxygen
dour means stern or hard

explanation.surface: A complaint that oxygen is difficult to detect by smell.
explanation.definitionFit: An odour is a scent or aroma, something perceived through the nose.

clue.text: Leaders remain by arrangement after church

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow the church abbreviation
the letters of remain are arranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Senior figures agree to stay on after a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by arrangement' rearranges REMAIN to AIRMEN, which comes 'after' CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Chairmen preside over boards and meetings, so they are heads of those bodies.

clue.text: Polished old Liberal economist

definitions.meaning: shining or burnished, as after rubbing
John ..., the Victorian Liberal statesman and free-trade campaigner

explanation.surface: A description of a refined Victorian Liberal thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: John Bright (1811-89) was a British Liberal politician famed for championing free trade and repeal of the Corn Laws.
explanation.definitionFit: Something polished gleams, i.e. is shiny; and John Bright was a famous nineteenth-century Liberal free-trader.

clue.text: He has been forced into private service

definitions.text: He has been forced into private service

parts.words: He has been forced into private service
parts.note: private looks like personal or domestic work, but a private is the lowest army rank, so this is someone compelled to join up

explanation.surface: Sounds like someone made to work as a household servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' suggests a butler's job; it is a soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: A man called up by law for military duty is drafted, made a soldier compulsorily.

clue.text: The gold edging makes this different

indicators.note: gold forms a border round the word the, so it wraps it

parts.note: OR is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: A gilt border sets this item apart from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edging' puts OR round THE. OR is gold in heraldry.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means not the same, distinct or alternative.

clue.text: 'Moody' could describe Romeo's disposition

indicators.note: read as dis-position, a placing of the letters differently, so Romeo's is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the S of the possessive included

explanation.surface: Romeo's temperament is summed up as moody, fitting a brooding lover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like temperament but signals rearranging ROMEOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy, as a moody person is.

clue.text: Money being paid for information

parts.note: L stands for pound sterling, from Latin libra, a unit of money
earning means receiving pay

explanation.surface: A complaint about having to pay for information.
explanation.walkthrough: L is the old sign for a pound (from Latin libra).
explanation.definitionFit: Learning is knowledge acquired through study, a body of knowledge.

clue.text: Comedian is second best

parts.note: the cream is the best part, as in the cream of the crop

explanation.surface: A verdict that a stand-up is only the runner-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' just links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A very funny person is informally called a scream, i.e. a hoot or riot.

clue.text: Submitted and faced the wall

definitions.meaning: handed in or presented, as an account or bill
coated brickwork with a layer of plaster or cement

explanation.surface: Someone gave in and turned to face the wall, as if punished.
explanation.definitionFit: To render a bill is to present it; to render a wall is to plaster its face.

clue.text: Government official needing change to dial PM

indicators.note: the letters of to dial PM must be changed into a new order

explanation.surface: A civil servant needs a new phone number to reach the Prime Minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges TO DIAL PM.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is a state's representative abroad, an envoy in its service.

clue.text: This affords light cover

parts.note: sounds like light protection, e.g. insurance or a thin blanket, but means a covering placed over a lamp bulb

explanation.surface: Sounds like a policy offering minimal insurance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light cover' suggests modest insurance; it is literally a cover for a light.
explanation.definitionFit: A shade fitted over a bulb literally covers a light.

clue.text: Strain through this business left with little hesitation

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a business
and means together with
er is a brief hesitation sound

explanation.surface: Someone strains with the effort of a business, hesitating briefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like effort but means sieving.
explanation.definitionFit: A colander is a perforated kitchen bowl used to drain food, a sieve.

clue.text: A dependant not paid to swallow annoyance

indicators.note: the unpaid abbreviation takes in the annoyance, enclosing it

parts.note: HON is short for honorary, describing a post held without pay
anger is irritation or annoyance

explanation.surface: Someone who relies on others has to put up with irritation without pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swallow' puts HON round ANGER. Hon. (honorary) means unpaid, as in honorary secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanger-on is a sycophantic follower who relies on someone else.

clue.text: The way a way may be found by a prison-reformer

parts.note: how means the way or manner
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A saying that a reformer will find a way, as where there's a will.
explanation.walkthrough: John Howard (1726-90) was an English campaigner for prison reform; the Howard League is named after him.
explanation.definitionFit: John Howard was an eighteenth-century English philanthropist who campaigned for better jails.

clue.text: Before midday completes making restitution

parts.note: AM means ante meridiem, before noon
ends means finishes or completes

explanation.surface: Someone finishes their atonement before noon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Amends are compensation for a wrong done, reparation.

clue.text: The most unhappy tot to be received by the school-head is French

indicators.note: the tot comes after the school's first letter, as if taken in by it

parts.note: the head, or first letter, of school is S
to tot up is to add
est is French for is

explanation.surface: A gloomy child is sent to the head teacher, who is French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tot' looks like a small child but means to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: Saddest is the superlative of sad, so most sorrowful.

clue.text: A flier requires warmth in clothing

indicators.note: the warmth goes inside the clothing word

parts.note: wear means clothes, as in menswear
heat means warmth

explanation.surface: A pilot needs warm clothes to fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flier' suggests a pilot, but it is a bird; 'in' puts HEAT inside WEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The wheatear is a small migratory songbird, a flying creature.

clue.text: Strange rites resulting in rows

indicators.note: strange means odd, signalling that rites is put in an odd order

explanation.surface: Weird ceremonies end in quarrels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rows' suggests arguments but means lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiers are ranks or levels, arranged one above another.

clue.text: Man is what no man is said to be

definitions.meaning: the Isle of Man, in the Irish Sea

definitions.text: what no man is said to be
definitions.meaning: John Donne's line No man is an ..., entire of itself

explanation.surface: A reflection on Donne's saying about human connection.
explanation.walkthrough: The Isle of Man lies between Britain and Ireland; Donne wrote No man is an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Man is an isle in the Irish Sea, and Donne's meditation says no person is a land mass cut off from others.

clue.text: A million diamonds in the Cape

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds

explanation.surface: A million pounds' worth of diamonds turns up in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Cape' suggests South Africa, but it is a garment. 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An amice is a liturgical vestment worn round the neck and shoulders, a kind of cape.

clue.text: Caution shown when there's conflict over a point

indicators.note: in a down clue the conflict sits above the point

parts.note: war is armed conflict
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A warning is issued when a dispute flares up over a minor issue.
explanation.definitionFit: To warn is to alert someone to danger, to put them on guard.

clue.text: About to appear in front of the first lady magistrate

indicators.note: the word for about comes before the first lady

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve, in Genesis the first woman

explanation.surface: A case concerning the President's wife comes before a judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first lady' suggests the President's wife; it is Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England, a chief magistrate of a town or district.

clue.text: He owes money to a painter who hasn't a bob — make a scene

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for debtor

indicators.note: the painter is without the coin, so it is removed

parts.note: Henri Matisse, the French painter
a bob was a shilling, abbreviated S

explanation.surface: A broke artist in debt causes a fuss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hasn't' takes S out of MATISSE, leaving MATISE. A bob was the British slang for a shilling, abbreviated s.
explanation.definitionFit: To dramatise is to adapt a story for stage, turn it into a scene.

clue.text: Antagonism will arise as men get rent altered

indicators.note: the letters of as men get rent are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Tenants grow hostile when landlords change rents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will arise' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Estrangement is alienation and hostility between people once close.
